text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITICAL NEWS RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The co-ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) will support advance payments under this year's harvests following a market analysis proving that it is necessary, Poland's Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said.

- The former president of the state-owned Television Wieslaw Walendziak will run for parliament on behalf of the right-wing Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) in the September elections, Walendziak said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland should quicken privatisation in key market sectors such as coal mining, chemical and steel industries, a report by the World Bank published on Wednesday said.

- European Leasing Fund (EFL) and the TU Europa insurance firm have bought a 51 percent share stake in the MR Leasing Service firm. Together with EFL the two leasing companies firms will control a 14.5 percent market share.

- A consortium led by the listed Bank Handlowy will buy a 75 percent stake in the Domy Towarowe Centrum, Poland's largest department store chain, following approval by the treasury ministry, Handlowy said.
- The Szczecin shipyard produced 18 ships worth 1.47 billion zlotys in 1996 showing an 11 percent upturn in terms of value compared with the year before, the yard said.

- Seven out of the world's ten biggest insurance brokerages have already opened branches in Poland. According to the Business Insurance professional monthly the companies are Marsh & McLennan Cos, Aon Group Inc, Sedgwick Group plc, Willis Corroon plc, Ja rdine Lloyd Thompson Group, CE Heath plc and Gras Savoye Sa.
- The listed Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) will rise interest rates on retail credits by two percentage points as of August 11, the bank said.

- The Powszechny Bank Kredytowy (PBK) to be privatised this year has presented additional documents to the share issue prospectus to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW), the HSBC Securities privatisation advisor Hubert Janiszewski said.
- Insurance firms may sell up to 20 million insurance policies in Poland which gives room for development to many new insurers, Nationale Nederlanden Poland president John Wylie said.

- The PTK Centertel analogue mobile telecom has contracted the EDS billing system services for the next five years, Centertel said. The contract allows for widening the scope of services in agreement with the operator's needs.
- The Dutch Campina Melkunie will be a strategic investor in the Grodzisk Wielkopolski dairy in western Poland and carry out the plant's modernisation.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Wolne Slowo publishing, which owns the conservative Zycie daily, will sell an up to 49 percent share stake in the company to a Warsaw-based company operating in a non-medial market sector, Wolne Slowo board member Wojciech Mikulecki said.
- The US's Goodyear tyre concern will build a new factory building at the site of its Polish subsidiary, the listed Debica tyre maker, to be completed in the first quarter of 1998, Debica said.
PARKIET
- The listed Warta insurance firm earned a net profit of 6.5 million zlotys in the first half of 1997, the company said.

- Bank Energetyki energy sector bank plans to up its share capital by 50 percent in the next nine months, the firm's president Slawomir Horbaczewski said. The bank's capital is now worth 55 million zlotys.
- The listed Polisa insurer made a net profit of 2.3 million zlotys in the first half off 1997, Polisa said.
